# Rendering and Post-Processing
## Overview
Rendering and Post-Processing handles the visual presentation of blocky voxel meshes generated by [Blocky meshing](31-blocky-meshing.md), addressing transparency artifacts and geometric jaggedness [G]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Greedy face merging](8935-greedy-face-merging.md) by operating on pre-generated geometry to optimize rendering order or refine surface topology, rather than modifying the initial [mesh extraction](#14720-mesh-extraction.md) topology [G].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Block Mesh Alpha Rendering](3569-block-mesh-alpha-rendering.md)
Sorts transparent chunk meshes back-to-front relative to the camera's dominant viewing axis to enable correct [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) without global depth sorting. Choose this for transparent voxel environments where performance is critical and full depth sorting is too expensive [G].

### [Quality Enhancement (Smoothing and Tessellation)](10395-quality-enhancement-smoothing-and-tessellation.md)
Refines blocky meshes using surface diffuse flow smoothing and Catmull-Clark tessellation to approximate smooth surfaces. Choose this when visual fidelity is prioritized over the raw voxel aesthetic [G].

### Ocean Mesh Rendering
Extends grid content to a flat area fitting the camera's view, typically used with displacement textures like Phoenix FD Ocean Texture [S1]. The ocean surface generates only when liquid touches the sides and bottom of the grid, which act as a container [S1]. Mesh detail depends on camera resolution: one or several polygons per pixel are generated based on the Ocean Subdivisions option [S1].

## Background
The techniques originate from fluid simulation post-processing in 3ds Max plugins (Phoenix FD) [S1]. Other methods in this family, such as chunk sorting and subdivision surface adaptation, originate from real-time rendering engines for voxel-based [games](#12542-games-gaussian-mesh-splatting.md) [G]. Not given in the sources for specific historical development.
